frozen_claims.text: On the method axis: their account holds that 129 primitive axioms; theorems derived from them; trika-x holds that finite tables; 332 `by decide` propositions; no axioms about the absolute. This matters because their theorems hold inside an assumed theology; ours hold inside an enumerated model.

On the self axis: their account holds that one witness-self; ego is superimposition (adhyasa); A4 makes Atman = Brahman an axiom; trika-x holds that self contracts through five named coverings; identity is never lost but is restricted. This matters because opposite formal treatment of plurality: error to be sublated vs real contraction.

On the recognition axis: their account holds that listed under 'what the formalization CANNOT capture': moksa is recognition, not a new state; trika-x holds that proved: recognition_adds_nothing, recognition_preserves_content. This matters because the single sharpest disparity: they call it unformalizable; we formalise it and they are the ones with axioms.

Their formalisation is: Advaita Vedanta: A Formal Axiomatization (Lean 4, scherf/Advaita) — 129 primitive axioms, 10 modules, master theorems TatTvamAsi + ThreeStateAnalysis (github.com/matthew-scherf/Advaita (README, retrieved 2026-11-17)). Recorded as published; not re-verified by this essay.
Our side is anchored in machine-checked structures: Recognition.lean :: recognition_adds_nothing, Kancuka.lean :: pairings_distinct. Registry references are not source-to-theorem entailments.
Shared ground: same target doctrine family (non-dual Kashmir/Advaita Shaiva-Vedantic).
Shared ground: recognition/moksa as non-production of a new state.

What it means: A paper can argue that 'recognition adds nothing' is formalisable without axioms, and that the Advaita axiomatisation's stated limitation is an artefact of its method, not of the doctrine.
